name: v5.39.0
body:
# What's New

This release helps you find what is safe to delete in the web UI, adds a working
trash on macOS, reports the space reflinked files really take up, and fixes a
number of disk usage miscounts. Below is a walkthrough of each change.

## Cleanup projections in the web UI

The treemap can now highlight what is safe to clean up. Use the projection
selector in the header (or press `P`) to switch the coloring. The tile area
always stays the size:

- **Location** - the default coloring by top-level directory.
- **Cleanup** - everything is grey except cleanup candidates. *Safe* ones are
  strong orange. These are regenerated by their tool, e.g. `node_modules` next
  to `package.json`, `target` next to `Cargo.toml`, `__pycache__`, the Go,
  Gradle, Cargo, npm, uv and Homebrew caches, and app caches. Ones to *review
  first* are muted gold: downloaded ML models, installed toolchains such as
  `~/.rustup` or `~/.nvm`, installers, virtualenvs, `dist`/`build` and
  git-ignored files.
- **Age** - colored by the latest change inside an item.
- **By category** - candidates in the current directory grouped by category, so
  cache space spread over many small directories shows up as one block.

The legend shows how much space each category takes. Click a category to
highlight only its items. Hovering a candidate shows what it is and how to
remove it cleanly (e.g. `ollama rm` for Ollama models). Candidates are found in
the background after the scan and are only highlighted. Deleting them is still
up to you.

Paths can be excluded and custom rules added in the `cleanup` section of the
config file:

```yaml
cleanup:
  exclude: [~/work/current-project]
  rules:
    - category: build-artifact
      confidence: safe
      dir: .gradle
      markers: [build.gradle, build.gradle.kts]
      hint: Rebuilt by Gradle
```

Deletion in the web UI now runs in the background. The item is drawn hatched
right away, you can delete more items and keep browsing in the meantime, and if
a deletion fails, the item comes back with the reason.

_by @mikhail-angelov in #697_

## Move to trash on macOS

The `D` key in the terminal UI and "Move to Trash" in the web UI now work on
macOS with no setup. Gdu runs the system `/usr/bin/trash` command, which moves
items into the Finder trash so you can put them back from there. It ships with
macOS 15 (Sequoia) and later. On older releases, gdu shows an error that points
you to `--trash-command`.

_by @mikhail-angelov in #698_

## Exclusive size for reflinked files

On filesystems with reflinks (XFS, btrfs, bcachefs, ...) several files can share
the same data. `stat` counts that shared data once for every file, so a
directory full of clones looks huge even though deleting it frees almost
nothing. The new `--exclusive-size` flag (Linux only) counts only the bytes a
file does not share with other files, which is what deleting it would free:

```
gdu --exclusive-size /some/dir
```

The figure replaces disk usage everywhere (sorting, bars, totals and the `dsize`
value in exports). Apparent size is unchanged. Exports gain an optional `shsize`
key with the shared bytes, which can also be selected with `--output-attrs`.
Where a filesystem does not support the needed `FIEMAP` call, gdu falls back to
the regular figure. See
[Reflinks and shared extents](https://github.com/dundee/gdu#reflinks-and-shared-extents)
for details.

_by @jamesbraid in #710_

## Unreadable directories marked in JSON exports

The JSON export used to look exactly the same whether the scan was complete or
not. A directory that gdu could not fully read is now written with
`"read_error":true` (the same key ncdu uses) and gets its `!` flag back when you
import the file. The key is written regardless of `--output-attrs`.

_by @jamesbraid in #712_

## Choose the shell opened with the b key

The shell spawned with the `b` key can now be set with `--shell` or in the
configuration file:

```
gdu --shell /usr/bin/fish
```

```yaml
shell: /usr/bin/fish
```

On Windows, gdu now stays open when you exit the shell instead of quitting.

_by @timbretimber in #722 and #721_

## More accurate disk usage

Several miscounts were fixed:

- **Directories** are now charged the blocks they really use, as `du` does. Small
  XFS directories stored inline report `0` instead of 4 KiB. On other
  filesystems, the directory's own blocks are added to the total. _(@shivampwm2020, #694)_
- **Hard links** in the scanned root directory are counted once, so the default
  non-interactive scan no longer reports up to twice the real usage. _(@mabunemeh, #709)_
- **Windows**: files compressed with NTFS compression and sparse files count
  their size on disk instead of their full length. _(@nk-batman21, #713)_
- **OneDrive online-only files** now show zero disk usage and keep their real
  apparent size. Previously it was the other way around. _(@AdamMagued, #692)_

## Better `--no-cross` (`-x`)

- `-x` no longer crosses into btrfs subvolumes and snapshots. Like `du -x`, it
  now skips any directory on a different device than its parent. _(@simon04, #711)_
- Mount points are found correctly when the scanned path is a symlink, such as
  `/Volumes/Macintosh HD` on macOS. _(@itssali, #705)_

## Non-interactive output fixes

- `sorting.by` and `sorting.order` from the configuration file are now honored
  in non-interactive listings, including `--depth`. `--reverse-sort` reverses
  the configured order. _(@kok-o, #703)_
- `--show-item-count` prints the same count as the TUI and web UI, whichever
  analyzer is used. _(@LuisFigueroaG, #691)_
- Empty and unreadable top-level directories are marked with `e` and `!`.
  _(@LuisFigueroaG, #716)_
